entries.topic: GDP per person, growth, population, inflation and trade, Israel and US, 1980-2025 (World Bank WDI)

claims.text: Book's arithmetic from the constant-dollar series: Israel's GDP per person as a share of the US level was 59.8% (1980), 56.9% (1985), 57.1% (1990), 60.5% (2000), 63.1% (2010), 64.4% (2019), 66.1% (2022), 62.6% (2024), 62.7% (2025). Average annual real growth per person 1980-2025: Israel 1.86%, US 1.75%; 1980-90 IL 1.88/US 2.35; 1990-2000 IL 2.76/US 2.18; 2000-10 IL 1.25/US 0.83; 2010-19 IL 1.86/US 1.62; 2019-25 IL 1.34/US 1.80. Israel's 2025 level was 0.1% above 2022.

World Bank population: Israel 3.878m (1980), 4.660m (1990), 6.289m (2000), 7.624m (2010), 9.215m (2020), 10.002m (2024), 10.123m (2025); US 227.2m (1980), 249.6m (1990), 282.2m (2000), 309.4m (2010), 331.6m (2020), 340.0m (2024), 341.8m (2025). Book's arithmetic: population growth averaged 2.2% a year in Israel and 0.9% in the US 1980-2025; real total GDP grew about 6.0 times in Israel and 3.3 times in the US

entries.topic: Israel's 1985 Economic Stabilization Plan and the US 1979-86 turn (Volcker, tax law); central banks

claims.text: Brookings (Bahar): in 1984 annualized inflation was about 400% (about 1,000% in the second half of 1984), the budget deficit about 17% of GDP; Peres formed a national unity government after the July 1984 election; the plan, led by Michael Bruno, cut the deficit by about 7.5% of GDP mainly by cutting food subsidies, devalued the shekel 20%, froze wages, prices and the exchange rate with pre-set adjustments, raised interest rates; Peres reached a wage agreement with the Histadrut; an American advisory group included Stanley Fischer; emergency US aid of about $750m a year (about 3.5% of GDP) for two years, conditional on reforms; monthly inflation fell from 11% (Q3 1985) to about 1% a year later; unemployment rose only about 2 points

Melnick and Mealem: the plan began in July 1985 with spending cuts, tax increases, abolished subsidies, a 'Non-Printing' law barring deficit finance by money creation, tight money, a government-Histadrut-employers wage package, temporary price controls and a fixed exchange rate after devaluation; US one-time grant of $1.5bn over two years; inflation about 20% by mid-1986; public debt about 163% of GDP in the mid-1980s and about 78% in 2008; public spending about 60% of GDP mid-1980s, about 43% end-2008; defence over 20% of GDP mid-1980s; public deficit about 14% of GDP in 1984 then surpluses; October 1983 banking crisis brought the economy close to financial collapse; 'the Stabilization Plan succeeded in achieving its two objectives'

Wikipedia: plan implemented 1 July 1985 under Peres; devised by Yitzhak Moda'i and Michael Bruno among others; measures included curbs on the Bank of Israel's ability to print money to cover deficits; inflation brought under 20% in less than two years; later reforms included 'the privatization of many government-owned businesses'

Federal Reserve History: on 6 October 1979 Volcker announced after an unscheduled FOMC meeting a shift from targeting the federal funds rate to the volume of bank reserves; the funds rate reached a record 20% in late 1980; severe recession; unemployment peaked at 10.8% in late 1982; inflation fell to 3.7% in 1983

Bank of Israel: under the Bank of Israel Law 2010 the primary goal is price stability; supporting economic activity and financial stability are secondary, pursued only if the Monetary Committee judges price stability will not be harmed; inflation target 1-3% set by government in 2000, in force since 2003; the 2024 review kept the range
Globes, 1 September 2026: Bank of Israel cut its rate 0.25 point to 3.25%, the fifth cut since November 2025, after cuts in late May and early July

Federal Reserve, 16 September 2026: FOMC raised the federal funds target range 1/4 point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, 12-0; 'Inflation remains elevated'; action 'will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal'; refers to the 'dual mandate'
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Peres won cabinet approval in a night-long meeting; Bahar cites Fischer's writing that the orthodox-heterodox mix 'may have been the key element of success'

Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Melnick and Mealem describe a decline in the Histadrut's labour-market influence from the early 1990s; unemployment rose to about 10% in the 2001-03 downturn; defence spending 'less than 10%' of GDP 'recently' (2009)

entries.topic: Taxes, who pays, deficits and debt: Israel and US over time

claims.text: OECD Revenue Statistics 2024 (Israel note): Israel tax-to-GDP 34.0% (2000, period high), 29.1% (2009, low), 32.8% (2022), 29.8% (2023); OECD average 32.9% (2000), 34.0% (2022), 33.9% (2023); Israel 2022 structure: personal income tax 22% of revenue (OECD 24%), corporate 13% (12%), social security 15% (25%), property 12% (5%), VAT 23% (21%)
OECD Revenue Statistics via DBnomics: US total tax revenue 23.6% of GDP (1965), 27.7% (2022, latest in the series); 1965-2022 range 22.9-28.3%, average 25.5%

Globes on Finance Ministry chief economist report (March 2022): Israel's tax burden 29.7% of GDP in 2020, 12 points of GDP below the 1986 peak; about half of those with income theoretically liable to income tax were below the threshold in 2021; direct tax rate on gross income about 40% for the top decile and 10% for the lowest; state tax revenue shares VAT 32%, income tax 30%, companies tax 12%; US burden cited as 25.5%

PwC (reviewed 29 June 2026): Israel 2026 top income tax bracket 47% above ILS 560,280; 3% surtax above ILS 721,560 brings the maximum to 50%; from 2025 an additional 2% surtax on capital income above that threshold

CBO (Jan 2026): 2022 average federal tax rate for all households 20.6% (1979-2022 average 20.9%); top quintile paid 70% of federal taxes (55% in 1979), top 1% paid 27% (14% in 1979); top 1% share of pre-tax-and-transfer income 9% (1979) to 18% (2022), after taxes and transfers 7% to 14%; average federal tax rate fell for every group 1979-2022, most for the lowest quintile; individual income tax rates about -10% (lowest quintile) to 17% (highest)

CBO (Feb 2026): FY2026 deficit $1.9tn (5.8% of GDP); debt held by the public 99% of GDP at end of 2025, 120% in 2036; passes the 1946 record of 106% in 2030; net interest $1.0tn (3.3% of GDP) in 2026, $2.1tn (4.6%) in 2036
OMB FY2009 Analytical Perspectives Table 16-1: US federal debt held by the public 26.1% of GDP (1980), 36.4% (1985), 42.0% (1990), 49.2% (1995), 35.1% (2000), 33.0% (2001), 36.8% (2007)
World Bank WDI central government debt: Israel 132.2% of GDP (1990), 117.8% (1991), 99.3% (1995), 88.3% (1999)
Israel's VAT rose from 17% to 18% on 1 January 2025, as part of an effort to rein in the deficit; estimated cost to families NIS 1,000-2,000 a year
World Bank WDI central government debt, US: 55.8% of GDP (2007), 76.0% (2009), 100.2% (2019), 124.5% (2020), 115.8% (2024) (series break around 2000-01)
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): direct tax rate on gross income about 30% for the second-highest decile

entries.topic: Israel's business groups and the 2013 Concentration Law; US industry concentration and antitrust; trade policy

claims.text: Times of Israel (10 Dec 2013): Knesset passed the concentration law with 72 votes for and one abstention; a 2010 Bank of Israel study found 30% of businesses part of pyramids and ten business groups controlling 41% of the market value of all public companies, Israel the most concentrated economy in the Western world per the study; holding companies limited to two levels, four to six years to spin off; names Tshuva (Delek owns Phoenix), Dankner (IDB: Cellcom, Supersol), Arison (Bank Hapoalim); Smoliansky: 'From now on, we will see pyramids only when we go to Egypt.'

Wikipedia: committee created 24 October 2010, interim report 11 October 2011, final recommendations February 2012; law passed December 2013 with 42 coalition and 30 opposition votes and no objections; new pyramids max two layers, existing reduced to three within four years and two within six; a controlling shareholder of a major real entity (turnover or credit above NIS 6bn) may not hold a major financial entity (assets above NIS 40bn); Finance Ministry list of 1,786 real-sector entities, 232 linked to IDB; IDB argued in 2011 there was no link between concentration and competitiveness

Delek Group sold 4.9% stakes in Phoenix to Mizrahi Tefahot and Bank Hapoalim (Aug-Sep 2018, NIS 509m total) to comply with the concentration law, holding 36.4%; completed divestment of a 32.5% stake to Centerbridge and Gallatin Point for NIS 1.57bn ($446m) in 2019 to comply

Grullon, Larkin and Michaely (2019): 'Since the late 1990s, over 75% of US industries have experienced an increase in concentration levels'; firms in industries with the largest increases show higher profit margins and more profitable M&A

ITIF (Kennedy, 2020) disputes the scale: in Census data 2002-2012 the top-four share fell or held in 319 of 792 six-digit industries (40%); studies find local concentration steady or falling (Rinz: about 25% fall 1976-2015); Grullon et al.'s results depend on the 1997 start (median HHI increase about 25% from 1972 instead of over 70%)

Kimmelman (HKS, June 2026): Judge Amit Mehta held Google illegally maintained a monopoly in general search through multi-billion-dollar default payments to Apple, Samsung, Mozilla and others; in the September 2025 remedies ruling he let Google keep paying for default placement with minimal restrictions

USTR: the US-Israel FTA, the first US free trade agreement, entered into force 1 September 1985; 2025 goods trade $34.4bn (US exports $13.7bn, imports $20.7bn, deficit $7bn); services trade $19.7bn; total $54.2bn
Globes (1 Aug 2025): US set a 15% tariff on Israeli goods, down from 17% announced 2 April 2025; Israel had expected 10%; Netanyahu's promise to cancel all tariffs on US imports not fully kept

Supreme Court, 20 February 2026, Learning Resources v. Trump (6-3, Roberts): IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; reciprocal tariffs voided; administration announced a 10% global tariff under Section 122 (capped at 15% and 150 days) and Section 301 investigations
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Delek also cited its business change and focus on energy; the swaps were 'similar to those contracted by IDB in Discount Investment Corporation' and by Clal Insurance
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): a 2016 committee set up by Kahlon and Governor Flug recommended that Hapoalim and Leumi sell their credit-card companies
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): 2025 US goods exports to Israel -7.2%, imports -6.6% vs 2024; services exports $9.7bn, imports $10.0bn, services deficit $337m
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Netanyahu's pledge to cancel all tariffs on US imports was only partly kept because of Israeli farmers' lobbying

Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Mehta cited windfall for Google, harm to distribution partners and disruption for consumers in declining to ban payments; the court itself called the search ecosystem 'exceptionally resistant to change'; Kimmelman: the conduct 'can continue largely unchecked'
